since_text: Thirty-five aeroplanes came onto the record today and all but one of them are Cessna 180s — this is the first sweep that actually went looking for them, and the 180 half of this market turns out to be thirty-six aircraft deep. The cheapest whole 180 flying is N4979A, the 1956 at Watsonville, California, $149,000 at 4,290 hours with one owner since 1991; the dearest is N889SL, the rebuilt 1958 180A at Justin, Texas, $325,000. Three of the new entries are not whole aircraft and are marked so on the row: a quarter share in a 1979 180 on straight floats at Renton, Washington for $85,000, a third share in a 1954 180 at Gig Harbor for $53,500 — the same seller offers a half share at $80,000 — and a 1953 project at Golf, Illinois for $105,000 with no logbooks. Nothing went today: no advertisement that was live this morning now reads sold. One figure in the record moved and it is a correction, not a cut — this record had been carrying N666SB, the 1980 A185F at Santa Paula, at $285,000, and the advertisement says $255,000, as FindAircraft does too. Two oddities worth knowing. The 1958 180A at $235,000 is advertised twice on Facebook, once from Caldwell, Idaho and once from Vancouver, Washington, by two different people; it is one aircraft, N58SD, and the Vancouver advertisement names it. And nobody agrees where the 1967 180H that Skywagons is brokering actually sits — the dealer's own page says Minnesota, Controller says Placerville California, Hangar67 says Illinois — and Controller prints its registration as N614JD where Trade-A-Plane, Barnstormers, FindAircraft, the dealer and the serial number all say N164JD. Three aircraft offered to this record were turned away: a 1958 “Cessna 182/180” at Santa Fe advertised in both 180 categories, which the register says is a 1957 Cessna 182A; a 1954 180 at $160,000 attributed to Skywagons, which is not on Skywagons' own inventory page; and a 1965 180H at $195,000 in Alabama carried by two aggregators whose only registration maps to a Cessna 182H.
provenance: Every source listed was reached. Facebook Marketplace is searched at fourteen cities with four search terms each and holds to roughly forty miles of each city whatever radius is asked for, so an ad far from all fourteen can be missed. aerogurus and FindAircraft repeat inventory other sites have sold or never carried, so nothing enters from either unless a primary advertisement or the dealer's own site confirms it. Eight listings carried here were not re-sighted this run and are flagged in the private record rather than silently folded in as unchanged.
